title: Mission of Saint Patrick
description: By tradition Patrick returns to Ireland as a missionary bishop in this year; the conversion of the island is in fact gradual.

title: First Viking raids
description: The annals record the burning of the island monastery of Rechru, the first Viking attack on Ireland.

title: Vikings settle at Dublin
description: Vikings build a fortified ship camp on the Liffey, the beginning of the town of Dublin.

title: Battle of Clontarf
description: The army of the high king Brian Boru defeats Leinster and its Viking allies, though Brian himself is killed.

title: Anglo-Norman landing
description: Norman knights land to restore Diarmait Mac Murchada to the kingship of Leinster, beginning English involvement in Ireland.

title: Henry II lands in Ireland
description: The English king arrives with an army and receives the submission of Norman lords and many Irish kings.

title: Edward Bruce invades
description: The brother of the Scottish king lands in Ulster and campaigns for three years as claimant to the high kingship before he is killed.

title: Statutes of Kilkenny
description: A parliament forbids the English settlers to adopt Irish language, law and custom, a sign of how far the colony had shrunk.

title: Poynings' Law
description: The Irish parliament is barred from meeting or legislating without the approval of the English king and council.

title: Henry VIII made King of Ireland
description: The Irish parliament turns the lordship into a kingdom held by the English crown.

title: Siege of Kinsale
description: The English defeat Hugh O'Neill and a Spanish force, the decisive battle of the Nine Years' War and the end of Gaelic Ireland's independence.

title: Flight of the Earls
description: The earls of Tyrone and Tyrconnell sail for the Continent with their followers and never return.

title: Plantation of Ulster
description: The crown begins settling the confiscated lands of the Ulster lords with Protestants from England and Scotland.

title: Rebellion of 1641
description: Catholic gentry in Ulster rise, thousands of settlers are killed, and eleven years of war follow.

title: Siege of Drogheda
description: Oliver Cromwell's army storms the town and kills the garrison and many townspeople at the start of his conquest of Ireland.

title: Battle of the Boyne
description: William III defeats the deposed James II, securing Protestant rule in Ireland.

title: Treaty of Limerick
description: The Jacobite army surrenders on terms and largely leaves for France; the promises made to Catholics give way to the penal laws.

title: Legislative independence
description: Under pressure from Henry Grattan and the Volunteers, Britain gives up its right to legislate for Ireland.

title: Battle of Vinegar Hill
description: Crown forces break the main rebel camp in Wexford, the turning point of the United Irishmen's rebellion.

title: O'Connell wins the Clare election
description: Daniel O'Connell is elected though as a Catholic he cannot sit, which forces Parliament to grant Catholic emancipation the next year.

title: Great Famine
place: Skibbereen, County Cork (among the worst-hit places)
description: Potato blight destroys the main food of the poor; about a million people die and at least a million emigrate.

title: Fenian Rising
description: A rising by the Irish Republican Brotherhood is quickly put down.

title: Land League founded
description: Michael Davitt and Charles Stewart Parnell found the league that leads tenant farmers in the Land War.

title: First Home Rule Bill defeated
description: The House of Commons rejects Gladstone's bill for an Irish parliament, splitting the Liberal Party.

title: Ulster Covenant
description: Nearly half a million unionists sign a pledge to resist Home Rule.

title: Easter Rising
description: Republicans seize the General Post Office and proclaim a republic; the execution of the leaders turns opinion towards independence.

title: First Dáil meets
description: Sinn Féin members elected in 1918 meet as an Irish parliament and declare independence, on the day the War of Independence begins.

title: Bloody Sunday
description: The IRA kills British intelligence officers in the morning, and in the afternoon police fire on a football crowd at Croke Park.

title: Civil War begins
description: The provisional government shells opponents of the Anglo-Irish Treaty in the Four Courts, beginning a civil war that lasts until 1923.

title: Constitution of Ireland
description: Éamon de Valera's constitution comes into force, replacing the Free State with a state named Ireland.

title: Republic of Ireland declared
description: Ireland becomes a republic and leaves the Commonwealth.

title: Battle of the Bogside
description: Three days of rioting lead to British troops being sent onto the streets of Northern Ireland, the start of the Troubles.

title: Bloody Sunday in Derry
description: British paratroopers shoot 26 unarmed civilians on a civil rights march, 14 of whom die.

title: Ireland joins the European Communities
description: Ireland enters the European Communities with the United Kingdom and Denmark.

title: International bailout
description: After the collapse of its banks Ireland accepts a rescue loan of 85 billion euros from the European Union and the IMF.

title: Marriage equality referendum
description: Ireland becomes the first country to approve same-sex marriage by popular vote.
